summary: Masaaki Sugiyama was a scholar of history, Central Asian studies, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1970 to 1979. He later taught at Kyoto Women's University from circa 1989 to 1992.
Masaaki Tsuchiya works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University from circa 1979 to 1989 and held a post at Senshu University around 1993.

Masaharu Anesaki was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University, working under scholars including Paul Deussen, and served as a professor and library director at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. After studying at Tokyo University of Education, he held an assistant professorship at Ibaraki University and became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba in 2006.

Masahide Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Tibetology. He studied at Nagoya University and the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later holding posts at Koyasan University, Nagoya University, and Kanazawa University.
Masahide Tsujimura specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at Kyoto University and served as an assistant professor at Kobe University in 2013.
Masahiro Asada is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1964 to 1974 and served there as an assistant professor from circa 1983 to 1990.

Masahiro Inami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed graduate coursework at Hiroshima University between circa 1983 and 1989 and held posts at Tokyo Gakugei University from circa 1993 onward.

Masahiro Kusunoki was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University from circa 1947 to 1953. He later served as a chair professor of religious studies and religious history at Tohoku University from circa 1973 to 1985.

Masahiro Shimoda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed degrees at the University of Tokyo, University of Tsukuba, and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo and later at Musashino University.
Masahiro Takano works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University between circa 1985 and 1991, where he was also attested as a librarian in 1995.

Masakatsu Fujita specializes in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1968 to 1975 and later served there as head of the Department of the History of Japanese Philosophy from circa 2003 to 2014.

Masakazu Tanaka is a scholar of religious studies who studied at Tohoku University and the London School of Economics. He served as an assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and vice president and professor at the Professional Institute of International Fashion (2019).

Masako Keta specializes in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi, and later held positions at Kanazawa University before serving as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University from 2000 to 2018.
Masamichi Asukai was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1952 to 1958 and held an academic post there from circa 1968 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao. He held professorships at Kyoto Sangyo University and Otani University, and served as president of Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, where he studied under Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 1991 and an assistant professor of literature in 2002.
Masanori Shono specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He is attested as an assistant professor at Osaka University in 2012 and as a researcher at the University of Munich in 2015.

Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, and held professorships at Kyoto University, Hanazono University, Nara University of Education, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
